title: Hannah and the Birth of Samuel
summary: Hannah, one of Elkanah's two wives, is barren and provoked by Peninnah. At Shiloh she prays silently and vows that if given a son she will give him to the LORD all his life. Eli, thinking she is drunk, rebukes her, then blesses her. She bears Samuel and, when he is weaned, brings him to Eli at Shiloh with a bull, flour and wine. Hannah prays a song of praise in which the LORD brings low and lifts up.

title: Eli's Sons and Samuel's Call
summary: Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas take the best of the sacrifices before the fat is burned and lie with the women at the tent door. A man of God warns Eli that his house will lose the priesthood and his two sons will die on one day. The boy Samuel, serving at Shiloh, hears a voice at night and thinks Eli is calling; Eli finally tells him to answer. The LORD tells Samuel he will judge Eli's house, and all Israel knows Samuel is a prophet.

title: The Ark Captured and Returned
summary: Israel is defeated by the Philistines and brings the ark from Shiloh, but is defeated again; 30,000 are killed, the ark is captured, and Hophni and Phinehas die. Eli, hearing the news, falls from his seat and dies, and Phinehas's wife names her newborn Ichabod. The ark topples the god Dagon and brings plague to Ashdod, Gath and Ekron, so the Philistines send it back on a cart with gold offerings. Men of Beth-shemesh who look into it die, and it is moved to Kirjath-jearim.

title: Samuel Judges Israel
summary: After twenty years of mourning for the ark, Samuel tells Israel to put away foreign gods and serve the LORD alone, and gathers the people at Mizpeh, where they fast and confess. When the Philistines come up, Samuel offers a burnt offering and cries out to the LORD, who thunders against them, and Israel pursues them. Samuel sets up a stone called Ebenezer, saying 'Hitherto hath the LORD helped us,' and judges Israel yearly from Beth-el, Gilgal, Mizpeh and his home at Ramah.

title: Israel Demands a King
summary: When Samuel's sons take bribes, the elders ask him for a king like other nations. Samuel warns what a king will take, but the people insist. The LORD points to Saul, a tall young Benjamite looking for lost donkeys; Samuel anoints him privately, then Saul is chosen by lot at Mizpeh and hides among the baggage. After Saul rescues Jabesh-gilead from Nahash the Ammonite, the kingdom is renewed at Gilgal, and Samuel gives a farewell address warning that king and people must fear the LORD.

title: Saul Rejected
summary: Facing the Philistines at Gilgal, Saul offers the burnt offering himself when Samuel is late, and Samuel tells him his kingdom will not continue. Jonathan's attack at Michmash, helped by a quake, routs the Philistines, and Saul nearly has Jonathan killed over a rash oath. Told to destroy Amalek completely, Saul spares King Agag and the best animals. Samuel says 'to obey is better than sacrifice,' kills Agag, and the LORD regrets making Saul king.

title: David Anointed
summary: The LORD sends Samuel to Bethlehem to anoint one of Jesse's sons. He passes over seven, including tall Eliab, with the words 'the LORD looketh on the heart,' and calls the youngest, David, from the sheep. Samuel anoints him, and the Spirit comes on David. Meanwhile the Spirit leaves Saul and an evil spirit torments him. His servants suggest a harpist, and David is brought to play for him, and Saul loves him and makes him his armor-bearer.

title: David and Goliath
summary: For forty days the Philistine champion Goliath of Gath, six cubits and a span tall in the KJV, challenges Israel to single combat. David, sent by Jesse with food for his brothers, hears the challenge, and Saul lets him go after he describes killing a lion and a bear. Refusing Saul's armor, David takes his staff, five stones and a sling, and answers Goliath 'in the name of the LORD of hosts.' He fells him with a stone and cuts off his head with Goliath's own sword, and the Philistines flee.

title: Saul's Jealousy and David's Flight
summary: Jonathan loves David and makes a covenant with him, giving him his robe and armor. Saul turns jealous at the women's song of 'Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands' and twice hurls a spear at David. He gives his daughter Michal to David for a bride-price of 100 Philistine foreskins, hoping David will die. Jonathan and Michal help David escape; David goes to Ahimelech at Nob, eats the showbread, and flees to Gath, where he pretends to be mad.

title: David in the Wilderness
summary: David gathers about four hundred men at the cave of Adullam. Saul, learning that Ahimelech helped David, has Doeg the Edomite kill eighty-five priests of Nob; Abiathar escapes to David. David saves Keilah and twice spares Saul, first in a cave at En-gedi, where he cuts Saul's robe, and later taking his spear and water jug in the camp at Ziph. Abigail brings food to David and persuades him not to kill her husband Nabal, who dies days later, and she marries David.

title: Saul and the Medium at Endor; Saul's Death
summary: As the Philistines gather, Saul, afraid, has the medium at Endor call up Samuel, who tells him that the LORD has become his enemy, the kingdom will pass to David, and Saul and his sons will die the next day. David, sent away by the Philistine commanders, returns to find Ziklag burned and the families taken; he pursues the Amalekites and recovers all. On Mount Gilboa the Philistines kill Jonathan and his brothers, Saul falls on his sword, and the men of Jabesh-gilead take back the bodies.
